The Gemini CLI uses a reason and act (ReAct) loop with your built-in tools and local or remote MCP servers to complete complex use cases like fixing bugs, creating new features, and improving test coverage.

I have been using this for about a month and it's a beast, mostly thanks to 2.5pro being SOTA and huge 1M context window. Other tools preemptively compress context or read files partially; this navigates large codebases effortlessly.

Gemini CLI at this stage isn't good at complex coding tasks vs. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, Qoder CLI, etc. Mostly because of the simple ReAct loop, compounded by relatively weak tool calling capability of the Gemini 2.5 Pro model.

The problem is that Gemini CLI simply doesn't work. Doesn't have a plan mode, jumps right into coding and then gets stuck in the middle of spaghetti code. Google is simply months behind Anthropic and OpenAI in this space!

I watched Gemini CLI hallucinate and delete my files: it ran mkdir which failed silently, then move commands sent files to an unknown location, and it 'lost' all the user's data with an apologetic breakdown message.

gemini-cli is completely useless for anything proactive... even if you ask it to just plan something, it'll run headlong into implementing unless you specifically tell it WITH ALL CAPS to not touch code. It could use a low level plan/act switch.
However, it does seem that Gemini pays less attention to security than Claude Code. Gemini will happily open in my root directory. Claude Code will always prompt 'Do you trust this directory?'

Please just give us a monthly subscription for developers that I can pay whatever, and then use Gemini CLI, this github action, Gemini chat, Jules, etc. Just like Claude and their max subscription. This would be a game changer for me.
